newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-DR J JOINS MAGIC FRONT OFFICE.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-DR J JOINS MAGIC FRONT OFFICE.

text.p: A day after wooing Hall of Fame coach Chuck Daly out of retirement, the Orlando Magic added a marquee name to the front office by naming Julius Erving the team's executive vice president.
Erving, known for soaring, creative and acrobatic play when Michael Jordan was still in grade school, also was given the title of vice president of RDV Sports, the company that owns the Magic.

"It is with great excitement and anticipation that we add a true living legend to our organisation as we continue in our pursuit of being the professional sports model of the 21st century," said Magic vice president and general manager John Gabriel.

"Dr. J brings a wide variety of experience and expertise -- both in the sport and the business of basketball -- to our club," Gabriel said. "From his playing days, which included championships, MVP honours and All-Star selections, to his various business involvements and community projects, Dr. J is synonymous with excellence."
Erving has been working as a television analyst for NBC's NBA coverage since 1993 and has done extensive community service work since his retirement in 1987.
He was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1993 after a 16-year career, including the first five as the premier player in the now defunct American Basketball Association.
He won championships in both leagues, averaged 24 points per game and scored 30,026 points -- the third-highest total in NBA history behind only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Wilt Chamberlain.
